# Coding Standards

## General Principles
- Write code that is simple, readable, and easy to maintain.
- Prefer clear naming over clever shortcuts.
- Keep functions and components small and focused on a single responsibility.
- Follow existing project patterns and structure.

## Consistency Rules
- Use consistent naming conventions across the codebase.
- Keep indentation, formatting, and file organization consistent.
- Avoid unnecessary duplication; reuse common logic where appropriate.
- Keep comments useful and minimal; explain intent, not obvious code.

## Maintainability
- Write code that is easy for another developer to understand quickly.
- Break large logic into smaller reusable pieces.
- Handle errors and edge cases gracefully.
- Keep business rules understandable and explicit.

## Quality Expectations
- Favor clarity over complexity.
- Make changes easy to review and test.
- Preserve existing behavior unless the change is intentionally improving it.
